assertions.description: Title/status, charge/summary, jobs, mode, priority, breakdown, balance, approval retain specified vertical order; title20 and charge28 have distinct visual hierarchy.
Match theme surface/text/muted/accent/ready/error palettes. Badge and shortfall use their status colors; selected mode and approval use accent with required contrasting foreground.
Read every required label and value; long content expands, wraps and stays associated. No clipping, truncation or overlap at supplied width/textScale.
Visible job checks, selected mode, priority persisted choice, disabled surfaces/labels and breakdown state match expected checkpoint state.
Card radius16, internal padding16, section spacing12, job vertical padding12, separator muted25%, approval radius10 and full inner width match reference intent.
Leading/trailing relationships and mode order mirror for RTL, including title/badge and job selection/text/price. English words and numbers remain readable.
Native parent scroller provides bounded overlapping evidence to actual content bottom for this state; no nested component vertical scroller or unreachable footer.
Physical touch region is separate from AX bounds. Verify actual native action target/hit evidence for this state; offscreen or unmeasured controls remain unassessed.

Exact SwiftUI font-tokens is not exported by public AX. Visual intent may be inspected separately; exact numeric values stay unassessed unless independently measured native pixel evidence supports them.

Exact SwiftUI padding-radius-separators is not exported by public AX. Visual intent may be inspected separately; exact numeric values stay unassessed unless independently measured native pixel evidence supports them.

limits: Full sweeps are the fixed two public checkpoints only. Missing target evidence is unassessed, not passed.
Disabled observer activations can establish disabled state but cannot establish exercised handler behavior.
SwiftUI AX frames do not measure physical hit regions, font sizes, padding or colors.
Manual visual judgments compare independent reference intent, not incidental y positions or renderer font rasterization.
